embedded-real-time-operating-systems--fi.title: open, read and close by descriptor
lines: ssize_t n = read(fd, buf, sizeof buf);
embedded-real-time-operating-systems--fi.note: fd indexes the process descriptor table; 0, 1 and 2 are already open as stdin, stdout and stderr.

embedded-real-time-operating-systems--io.title: shell redirection with dup2
lines: int fd = open("out.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
dup2(fd, STDOUT_FILENO);   /* entry[1] now names out.txt */
close(fd);                 /* the extra descriptor is spare */
printf("hello\n");         /* lands in the file, not the tty */
embedded-real-time-operating-systems--io.note: dup2 copies one descriptor-table entry over another, so fd 1 and fd share one open file description and its offset.

embedded-real-time-operating-systems--pr.title: dividing the PIT clock down to a 100 Hz tick
lines: outb(0x40, divisor >> 8);         /* high byte; tick every 10 ms */
output: divisor 11931 gives 100.007 Hz, a 9.999 ms tick
embedded-real-time-operating-systems--pr.note: The counter divides a fixed input clock, so the reload value alone sets the tick period and the periodic interrupt rate.
